content.title: Reply to R3 (wo3E)
content.comment:
**R3.1.** The novelty of the proposed method is not significant. From my understanding, the proposed method falls into the category of Bootstrapping, i.e. it uses a model to generate the pseudo labels to train a new model. Although the method shows promising performance, it basically shows that bootstrapping strategy is useful for this task. 

**A3.1.** It is not only bootstrapping. The novelty of our approach is to introduce retrieval into self-training. Bootstrapping gives only 44% (see section 5.3 effect of retrieval step) as opposed to REST achieving 63%.


**R3.2.** The author proposes a new error metric to evaluate their performance, which is questionable. The new error metric is using the CLIP text encoder, which is also part of the proposed method as the retrieval in section 3.4. In other words, the proposed method REST is optimized by the CLIP model and then it is evaluated by the CLIP model. And the author only provides this new error metric as the only measurement for all experiments.

**A3.2.** This is not correct. We do not evaluate our model based on some sort of similarity score produced by CLIP. We evaluate based on top-1 accuracy on novel classes as other papers. As our method produces free-form sentences, we only use CLIP’s text encoder to map free-form captions to class labels.

**R3.3.** For the user study, the author did not mention how many human annotators are and how they are being recruited. The quality of annotators could affect the result.

**A.3.3.** The videos present in Kinetics describe generally well known concepts and don’t require a particular form of domain expertise. The annotators were graduate students or professionals with full English proficiency.  We used 8 annotators. We followed Leveinboim et al, 2019 which showed that 8-10 annotators produce a reliable score for evaluation of vision-text data.

We hope that we have addressed your concerns and that you will be able to increase your recommendation toward acceptance. We are more than happy to provide any additional clarifications.

content.title: Reply to R2 (UrMu)
content.comment:
We thank the reviewer for recognising the novelty of our approach and the advantages of the unsupervised adaptation method proposed. We hope that we have addressed your remaining concerns below.

**R.2.1.** The generative model didn't produce better results than the discriminative ones. Compared with full supervision, unsupervised adaption still have a large gap to catch up. While on zero/shot, it competes with but is not better than the supervised one. 

**A.2.1.** Full supervision outperforms our method only when training and testing is on the same dataset (i.e. Kinetics; table 1).  On zero-shot we’re better than ALL discriminative methods but  X-CLIP (ECCV 2022; arxiv submission at the time of submission, which we could have ignored per the ICLR rules) which we outperform on HMDB (table 2) and on the generalised zero-shot Kinetics (table 4). Downgrading the impact of our approach on the grounds of not outperforming discriminative methods on **all** databases is discouraging for those aiming to develop new methods. 

**R.2.2.** The experiments didn't show any other advantages of the generative model. The discriminative models can also fulfill all the provided tasks. So the motivation for developing such a generative model is questionable. 

**A2.2.** As mentioned in paragraph 1 of intro a “generative approach has practical advantages including producing more fine-grained (compared to an action class label) and more interpretable/human-readable output, and being naturally more open-world (compared to contrastive learning based approaches) in a sense that it does not require a priori definition of the action classes” (for example CLIP requires the list of 1000 ImageNet classes to produce the zero-shot results). 
This is the motivation behind our work. 

**R.2.3.** In my opinion, retrieval is crucial for achieving such a good performance in video recognition. It lacks the results of the model without any retrieval steps. This is related to the configuration of the dataset Kinetics-400, which has hundreds of videos for each class. With Kinetics-400, the retrieval steps can easily obtain the video or captions from the same category, making retrieval especially useful.

**A2.3.** We report the impact of performance as a function of the number of retrieval steps in Table 7a (59.16% for N=1 BS 63.95 for N=4). If the retrieval component isn’t used at all (N=0), the performance drops to only 44% (see section 5.3 effect of retrieval step). Importantly, the novelty of our approach is to introduce retrieval into self-training. We will also add the result for N=0 to the table.

We hope that we have addressed your concerns and that you will be able to increase your recommendation toward acceptance. We are more than happy to provide any additional clarifications.

content.title: Reply to R1 (xKKd)
content.comment:
We thank the reviewer for recognising the novelty of our approach and of the direction that it opens - that of open-vocabulary video recognition, hence we were a bit surprised by the low rating. We hope to have addressed your concern below and we remain available to clarify and reply to any additional questions.

**R.1.** REST did not compare with state-of-the-art zero-shot action recognition methods.

**A.1.** We compare against current state-of-the-art zero shot recognition models on UCF-101 and HMDB-51 (Table 3), and Kinetics-220 (Table 4). We also included comparisons with X-CLIP (ECCV 2022), an arxiv submission at the time of ICLR submission, which we could have ignored per the ICLR rules. We would be happy for the reviewer to point us to missing works on zero-shot action recognition to further improve our manuscript.

We hope that we have addressed your concerns and that you will be able to increase your recommendation toward acceptance. We are more than happy to provide any additional clarifications.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This work proposes the first method called REST to adapt a generative V&L FM for open-vocabulary action recognition. REST contains two key components including an iterative Self-training without using any action-specific labels and a CLIP-based Retrieval to discover a diverse set of pseudo-captions to train the model. REST achieves competitive performance compared with CLIP-based methods on UCF-101 and HMDB50.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
- This work is the first work to develop a generative V&L FM for open-vocabulary video recognition. I believe that it's a very meaningful attempt for the community. 

- The self-training procedure for REST does not need any action-specific labels. The REST can be also trained without any labels in an unsupervised manner.


Weakness:
- REST did not compare with state-of-the-art zero-shot action recognition methods.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Overall, the reviewer agrees that the work tackles an essential problem for video recognition. However, several parts require further justifications by the authors to conclude the contributions of the work.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper aims to tackle the action recognition methods using Vision& Language Foundation Model. Instead of employing a discriminative model as recently appeared work, this approach aims to accomplish this task using a generative model. This work found that directly fine-tuning a generative model to the action recognition domain will suffer an overfitting problem. Therefore, it proposed an unsupervised method, which includes (1) a pseudo-caption generation and self-training strategy. (2) a retrieve module to preserve the diversity of the training samples. The method reports competitive results on the zero-shot/few-shot setting.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengthen:
+ Using the generative model for action recognition is new. It presents better interpretability.
+ Unsupervised domain adaption for action recognition also saves annotation labor. 

Weakness:

- The generative model didn't produce better results than the discriminative ones. Compared with full supervision,  unsupervised adaption still have a large gap to catch up. While on zero/shot, it competes with but is not better than the supervised one. 

- The experiments didn't show any other advantages of the generative model. The discriminative models can also fulfill all the provided tasks. So the motivation for developing such a generative model is questionable. 

- In my opinion, retrieval is crucial for achieving such a good performance in video recognition. It lacks the results of the model without any retrieval steps. This is related to the configuration of the dataset Kinetics-400, which has hundreds of videos for each class. With Kinetics-400, the retrieval steps can easily obtain the video or captions from the same category, making retrieval especially useful.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Using the pseudo-caption for unsupervised domain adaption is novel.
The necessity and reusability of the proposed method in the action recognition domain are questionable. 
The paper is clear enough to be reproduced.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper contains apparent novelty in utilizing a generative model for action recognition. However, the superiority of using such a method for the action recognition problem is unclear. The reusability of the method for another dataset is also questionable. In my current opinion, the method is novel but is not practical for action recognition. The author should present more superiorities of the proposed REST.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes using the pseudo label to train a caption generation model for video clips. The proposed backbone model is mainly based on previous work BLIP. This paper's main contribution is adapting the BLIP model for video clip caption generation with zero-shot and few-shot training.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
- This paper has a certain novelty. The proposed method is the first one for adapting a generative model for open-vocabulary action/video recognition. The author proposes a method of generating the pseudo labels for a video clip in section 3.3. The proposed video-text retrieval is proven to be effective in the experiment. 

-  The proposed method achieves leading performances as shown in the experiment section. In Tab. 2, the proposed method achieves better results than these out-of-the-shelf methods, although worse than the fully-supervised methods. In Tab. 3, the proposed method achieves the best performance in the HMDB-51 datasets and the Kinetics-220 dataset.

- The author provides the ablation studies to show the effectiveness of the retrieval step, number of cached captions and number of retrieval steps. The structure of the experiment section is reasonable.

Weakness:
- The novelty of the proposed method is not significant. From my understanding, the proposed method falls into the category of Bootstrapping, i.e. it uses a model to generate the pseudo labels to train a new model. Although the method shows promising performance,  it basically shows that bootstrapping strategy is useful for this task. 

- The author proposes a new error metric to evaluate their performance, which is questionable. The new error metric is using the CLIP text encoder, which is also part of the proposed method as the retrieval in section 3.4. In other words, the proposed method REST is optimized by the CLIP model and then it is evaluated by the CLIP model. And the author only provides this new error metric as the only measurement for all experiments.

Clarification:
- For the user study, the author did not mention how many human annotators are and how they are been recruited. The quality of annotators could affect the result.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is well-written and I can understand the method clearly. The method is easy to re-implemented. The proposed method has a certain of novelty but is not significant as I wrote in the above comments.
content.summary_of_the_review: The proposed method has shown good performance in multiple datasets that reflect the effectiveness of the proposed method. However, it is hard for me to appreciate the novelty of the proposed method, and I hope the author could clarify my concerns about the evaluation metric.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper proposes to adapt a pretrained generative Vision & Language (V&L) Foundation Model for video/action recognition.

They also introduce REST, a training framework consisting of (i) an unsupervised model for adapting the generative model to action/video through pseudo-caption generation and self-training mechanism and (ii) a retrieval approach based on CLIP for discovering a diverse set of pseudo-captions for each video to train the model.

They evaluate the proposed model on zero-shot action recognition and compared to some contrastive learning-based methods.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
[strength]

- Well motivated in the Introduction section & the latest works are cited/discussed in the paper

- Some good evaluations in the experimental section

[weakness]

Major:

- The novelty is very limited as the proposed model seems to be based on two pre-trained models e.g., CLIP & BLIP with the added temporal adapter as well as the retrieval module. Refer to following comments for more details.

- Why table 1 only shows your proposed model, it should add other generative models into comparison. Maybe only your method obtain such bad results and have you compared to other existing generative models?

- The authors claim in Introduction last paragraph `such an approach is label-free making it potentially suitable to be applied to any large-scale video dataset'. However, your proposed model requires pseudo-captions as well as additional pseudo-captions are used to improve the performance, how can it be suitable compared to dataset with labels e.g., pseudo-label, would it be easier than your model? There are also no comparisons in terms of timing, parameters, & model complexity etc.

- The authors listed some existing methods in the related work section which are either treated as baselines e.g., BLIP & CLIP (they only appear in one table and totally disappeared in the rest tables, why?) or very closely related to the proposed model  e.g., Chen et al (2021), Wang et al (2021) and Castro & Heilbron (2022), these models are not fully investigated, discussed/analyzed/compared in the experimental section to support the claims made in the listed contributions.

- Section 3.2 and 3.3 show `causal attention', if this is not proposed by the authors, then citations should be put (might also be discussed in related work section if it is closely related to your work). Your readers are very confusing especially the writing/descriptions in the Method section.

- Figure 1 caption, the authors say that 'adding only a lightweight temporal adapter', and in text, 'by inserting a temporal adapter in-between the layers of BLIP's spatial visual transformer', what do these mean? Between which layers? There are '12 transformer layers' as the authors mentioned in section 3.2, so this temporal adapter can be added anywhere? More detailed descriptions should be added either in figure caption or in text if this is an innovation. Ambiguous is not your friend, the readers are very interested in every piece of technical details, so please be kind and be clear.

Note that simply releasing the codes is absolutely not a whole replacement of a detailed, well-organized descriptions in the paper.

- The authors mention that `The adapter layer is initialized such that the temporal residual, introduced by it, will be of low magnitude initially, closely aligning the network's output early on to that of the pre-trained image model'. I do not understand what does this mean and how. Please make your statements clear enough to readers.

- The organization inside Method is a bit messy, it would be better to re-order them and make it well-organized to readers.

- Only numerical results are provided and no any figures or visualizations to show e.g., comparisons, model weights visualizations/comparison or effectiveness of REST/temporal adapter, and proposed models versus the contrastive learning-based models etc. Comparisons such as timing/model sizes/complexity would be better to show the effectiveness of the proposed model.

- Evaluation section a bit messy, looks like a mixture of many different evaluations, it should have better ways to re-organize them and make them clear enough.

- Section 5.1 of few-shot experiments, 'we finetune the trained models directly using the class names', what does this mean? Class labels or encoded class names? A bit confusing and not clear to me.

- Section 5.2, the authors evaluate different types of supervision; however, these models are not grouped & discussed in related work section. This should be closely related to the proposed model.

- Table 2 -- a good table, I like it. Why only pre-trained on Kinetics-400 rather than on other datasets e.g., the one used by the baseline models CLIP-400M & LAION-115M. Note that these datasets are used in the baselines of BLIP & CLIP, would be better to have a fair comparison among them rather than pre-trained on a different dataset. Maybe if CLIP/BLIP/X-CLIP if pre-trained on the same dataset with unsupervised adaptation would give better results to your proposed model? Or the authors think this would definitely not happen hence not worth investigating?

- The discussions are very limited in the experimental section e.g., evaluation on HMDB-51/UCF-101/Kinetics-400. Discussion and analysis of the results are more important and interesting to readers than recording/describing numerical results. It would be better to show some deep insights from your analysis that the readers do not know from the tables. What do you think?

- In 'evaluation on Kinetics-220', why 'under this setting, our model is only surpassed by the concurrent work of Ni et al 2022'? Any discussions? `Ni et al 2022' should be discussed/analysed as well as in comparisons (simply list it in the table and I can see their method is ~5% better than yours). 

- The authors say that `CLIP, due to being trained on a very large dataset, performs the best', this is not a solid reason that the proposed model unable to beat it. The issue I noticed is that both models are not trained on the same dataset to show the effectivess of the proposed model, and it is not a fair comparison.


Minor:

- Abstract section: missing point (a), I found point (b) listed but no `(a)'.

- Table 1 too long caption, more descriptions can be added in the text rather than putting the whole paragraph in table caption.

- `Training efficiency' can be a separate paragraph.

- Section 5.1 `224 x 224px' spelling mistake or typo?

On a separate note, please do not cite too many arXiv papers.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
- Writing quality is below the acceptance bar, especially in Method section.

- Novelty is limited (also due to poor writing), the proposed model is only based on two pretrained model e.g., BLIP & CLIP and added a temporal adapter and a retrieval model (but the details of these two models especially the temporal adapter is not fully described e.g., `by inserting a temporal adapter in-between the layers of BLIP's spatial visual transformer', but how?).

- The organization of the paper needs to be improved, especially the method section.

- Reproducibility: Given the current raw paper I do not think it is able to reproduce the experimental results.

Note that simply releasing the codes is absolutely not a whole replacement of a detailed, well-organized descriptions in the paper.
content.summary_of_the_review:
Overall the paper suffers from the following issues:

- I do not think the novelty is enough to meet this venue as mentioned in weakness section.

- The writing quality is below the acceptance bar, especially in the method section. Further issues appear in experimental section, and the descriptions of the evaluation protocols are too messy.

- Only numerical results in the form of tables and no any figures/visualizations to show the effectiveness of the proposed model e.g., the temporal adapter or REST module (note that I have checked the appendix and the visualizations are also very limited).

- The authors listed some existing works in the related work section which are either treated as baseline models or closely related to the proposed model; however, these models e.g., BLIP & CLIP, Chen et al. 2021, Wang et al. 2021 & Castro & Heilbron 2022 are not evaluated/compared in the experimental sections (e.g., tables, etc) 

Hence, I put my score at Reject unless (i) clearly stated reasons for raised issues are provided and (ii) if exist factual errors. Please address all the raised issues (major + minor) one by one, point to point, and clear in rebuttal.

content.title: REST: REtrieve & Self-Train for generative action recognition
content.abstract: This work is on training a generative action/video recognition model whose output is a free-form action-specific caption describing the video (rather than an action class label). A generative approach has practical advantages like producing more fine-grained and human-readable output, and being naturally open-world. To this end, we propose  to adapt a pre-trained generative Vision & Language (V&L) Foundation Model for video/action recognition. While recently there have been a few attempts to adapt V&L models trained with contrastive learning (e.g. CLIP) for video/action, to the best of our knowledge, we propose the very first method that sets outs to accomplish this goal for a generative model. We firstly show that direct fine-tuning of a generative model to produce action classes suffers from severe overfitting. To alleviate this, we introduce REST, a training framework consisting of two key components: an unsupervised method for adapting the generative model to action/video by means of pseudo-caption generation and Self-training, i.e. without using any action-specific labels; (b) a Retrieval approach based on CLIP for discovering a diverse set of pseudo-captions for each video to train the model. Importantly, we show that both components are necessary to obtain high accuracy. We evaluate REST on the problem of zero-shot action recognition where we show that our approach is very competitive when compared to contrastive learning-based methods. Code will be made available.
